rules.sentence: Grade I is characterized by purely subjective symptoms, eg, paresthesia, without motor deficits.
Grade II involves muscle weakness or objective sensory findings, subdivided into IIA, with no intrinsic muscle atrophy, and IIB, with some atrophy of the intrinsic muscles.
Grade III presents with pronounced sensory and motor deficits accompanied by marked atrophy of the intrinsic muscles.
The prognosis for mild ulnar neuropathy is generally favorable, with early intervention critical to prevent progression.
Conservative treatment is indicated for patients with mild-to-moderate symptoms.

In patients with mild symptoms, nonoperative management has demonstrated benefit in approximately 90% of cases, whereas only 38% of patients with moderate symptoms respond adequately to conservative measures.

In untreated mild and moderate cases of UNE, approximately one-half of patients reported symptom improvement, although activity modifications, eg, avoiding prolonged elbow flexion or repetitive movements, may have contributed to recovery.
Negative prognostic factors include high occupational force demands, smoking, obesity (BMI ≥30 kg/m²), female sex, and distal upper-extremity fractures.
